description.en: standard PIT rate higher PIT tax rate highest PIT tax rate  Sets the standard/base personal-income-tax rate (20%), applied to employment income and most other income types up to the relevant annual threshold (60 AMS pre-2026; 36 AMS from 2026), per the LT tax summary and country-report Table 2.17. It is used extensively across both the withholding policy (tin_admn_lt/ArithOp, BenCalc) and the final-tax-liability policy (tin_lt/ArithOp, BenCalc, SchedCalc's 'PIT SCHEDULE - FINAL'), and is also referenced in the self-employed social-insurance-contribution policy tscse_lt/BenCalc as part of the contribution-base calculation. Sets a 25% personal-income-tax rate, the new intermediate band introduced under the LT PIT reform effective 2026: for most income types, 20% applies up to 36 average monthly salaries (AMS) per year, 25% between 36 and 60 AMS, and 32% above 60 AMS, per the LT 2025-2026 tax summary. It is used in tin_admn_lt/ArithOp's Formula ('PIT taxed at 25 percent') and as a Band_Rate in tin_lt/SchedCalc's final PIT schedule. Sets the top marginal personal-income-tax rate (32%), applied to income above 60 average monthly salaries (AMS) per year under both the pre-2026 and 2026 rate structures described in the LT tax summary and the country report's Table 2.17. It is used in tin_admn_lt/ArithOp's Formula (flagged not applicable from 2026) and as a Band_Rate in tin_lt/SchedCalc's final PIT schedule.

explanation.en: Assembled from params.parameter_groups LT:ConstDef_lt:tin_schedule (band 1 rate=euromod://LT/ConstDef_lt/def_const/$tin_StdRate, band 2 rate=euromod://LT/ConstDef_lt/def_const/$tin_HigherRate, band 3 rate=euromod://LT/ConstDef_lt/def_const/$tin_HighestRate). EUROMOD's role is upper_threshold; brackets carry the band's lower bound.
